approach: Add a new immutable record `athena.hestia-sweep/1` in athena-data (HestiaSweep, HestiaCheckResult, HestiaFinding) following the Audit pattern. In athena-core, hestia.rs re-exports them as Sweep/CheckResult/Finding, defines a Check trait and run_sweep (a check Err becomes a Finding by code; later checks still run), plus Athena::hestia_sweep and last_sweep. The CLI gets `athena hestia sweep` and `athena hestia last`; the text renderer lives in the existing athena-cli/src/lib.rs (a deliverable) so it is unit-tested without new files. The trigger is an explicit command, with a drain hook deferred. D129 is marked accepted, with a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Trigger is an explicit command (`athena hestia sweep`, `athena hestia last`); drain hook deferred.
decisions.reason: No timer or daemon exists; a command is testable and keeps the report-only role off the drain path (D127: Hestia never gates work).

rejected.why: Couples a report-only role to the work path and slows drains; can be added later on the same function.

decisions.choice: Store each sweep as one record `athena.hestia-sweep/1` at records/hestia-sweeps/<YYYY-MM>/<id>.json holding check results and findings.
decisions.reason: Matches audits and ratings; `last` is a read of the newest record; counts for clean checks stay listed.

rejected.why: Cannot list checks with zero findings.

decisions.choice: Types live in athena-data as HestiaFinding etc.; hestia.rs re-exports as Finding.
decisions.reason: athena-data is a leaf crate; avoids clash with the existing verification Finding there.

decisions.choice: Check Err becomes a Finding in run_sweep and the entry is marked errored; the sweep continues.
decisions.reason: Mechanism, not convention; a failed check never looks like a clean 0.

decisions.choice: Answer to findings 3 and 4: drop the new files crates/athena-cli/src/hestia.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests/hestia.rs. Put the renderer and its tests in the listed crates/athena-cli/src/lib.rs, with wiring in main.rs. The CLI test calls the renderer for both cases (none recorded, and a sweep with a finding); the wiring is shown by running `cargo run -- hestia last`.

rejected.option: New cli module and integration test file
rejected.why: Outside the deliverables list; widens scope.

decisions.choice: Answer to finding 2: keep a small edit to crates/athena-core/src/store.rs (add hestia_sweeps to Records::load), and name it as a necessary addition outside the list.
decisions.reason: Records::load matches AnyRecord exhaustively, and an unlisted variant reaches its 'names its job' panic arm. `last_sweep` also reads through it.

rejected.option: Have hestia.rs read record files directly
rejected.why: Bypasses the one loader and duplicates its parsing and ordering.

decisions.choice: Empty default check list; `sweep` prints 'no checks registered' and `last` prints 'no sweep recorded' when none exist.

rejected.why: Would pass as a real check.

risks.risk: New AnyRecord variant hits the Records::load fallback panic.
risks.mitigation: Add the load arm and the path/schema arms together; a core test commits and loads a sweep.

risks.risk: A failed check looks like a clean 0.
risks.mitigation: errored flag in the record and a printed marker, with a renderer test.

risks.risk: Scope creep into real checks or a drain hook.
risks.mitigation: Keep to the file list; default_checks is empty.

risks.risk: Doc text trips the boundary or personal-data scan.
risks.mitigation: Use plain words and no emails; cargo test runs the scan.

risks.risk: Name clash with the existing Finding in records.rs.
risks.mitigation: Use HestiaFinding in athena-data and alias it in athena-core.

demonstrations.method: Unit test with three fake clean checks run through run_sweep.
demonstrations.observes: All three ids are listed with count 0 and the findings list is empty.
demonstrations.fails_without: If run_sweep dropped clean checks from the report, the assertion that every id appears with count 0 would fail.

demonstrations.method: Unit test with one erroring check, one check with a real finding and clean ones.
demonstrations.observes: One finding for the failing check (check id, subject, evidence containing the error text, age, state open); entry marked errored; the other checks are listed with their counts.
demonstrations.fails_without: If an Err were propagated or ignored, the test would fail on the missing finding or on run_sweep returning an error.

demonstrations.method: Record tests: to_json then parse at the canonical path gives an equal sweep; the path is records/hestia-sweeps/<month>/<id>.json; validate rejects mismatched counts and duplicate ids. A core test (cargo test -p athena-core hestia) commits two sweeps and checks last_sweep returns the later.
demonstrations.observes: Round-trip equality, rejection cases, and the newest sweep returned.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the AnyRecord variant, validate or the load path were missing, parse or last-selection would fail.

demonstrations.method: Tests in athena-cli/src/lib.rs call the renderer for no sweep and for a sweep with a finding. Also exercise `cargo run -- hestia last` in a repository with and without a sweep.
demonstrations.observes: 'no sweep recorded' when none exists; otherwise each check with its count and each finding with all five fields.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `last` printed nothing on empty records, the 'no sweep recorded' assertion would fail; a missing finding line would fail the second test.

demonstrations.method: Tests build athena_core::hestia::Finding with all five fields; git diff shows `pub mod hestia;` in lib.rs.
demonstrations.fails_without: The test would not compile if a field or the export were missing.

demonstrations.observes: D129 heading and Status say accepted, decided by the brain under Sri's delegation (BRIEF.md addenda 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-26); the trigger and alternatives are stated; the 'not accepted; build jobs not queued' wording is gone; D130 is unchanged.
